context: Music festival Lost & Found station; Fusion challenge prototype

pageCopy.title: Lost & Found locker
pageCopy.intro: Built for a festival Lost & Found station, this Arduino prototype uses RFID tags to identify items and respond to claims with a display, LEDs, a buzzer and a servo-controlled lock.
pageCopy.demoLabel: Browser demonstration based on the archived Arduino sketch. Sample item data.

explicitSketchConnections.note: Passed as MFRC522's first constructor argument; do not confuse the reader board's SDA label with LCD I2C SDA.

softwareBehavior.registration: Master card, item-tag scan, description read through Serial Monitor, fixed owner assignment, record appended, unlock for placement.
softwareBehavior.claim: Recognized personal tag is compared against itemOwners. First matching item unlocks, then is removed from arrays.
softwareBehavior.unknownTag: Access Denied, 500 Hz tone for 500 ms, red LED flashes three times with 500 ms on and 500 ms off.
softwareBehavior.successfulUnlock: Green LED high, 1000 Hz tone for 500 ms, servo 0 degrees for 8 seconds then 90 degrees, green LED low.

presentationRules: Use the real cardboard enclosure and black-painted build as evidence.
Label simplified machine art and browser behavior as illustrative.
Do not claim the servo automatically swings the door; the footage shows a person opening it.
Use original source excerpts instead of reproducing the photographed early code draft.
Keep dispenser media separate; a background dispenser in a locker photo is not locker hardware.
Keep real source timings and edited-video timings distinct.
Describe captions as explanatory visual descriptions, not a transcript of speech.
